# Jam-a-Lot

> Jam-a-Lot is a browser-based jazz practice application. It plays synthesized acoustic drums, double bass, and electric piano accompaniment over jazz standard chord charts while displaying interactive lead sheets.

## Documentation & AI Access
- [User Manual](https://app.jam-a-lot.org/manual.html): Complete user manual detailing playback controls, performance planning, chord charts, instrument mixer, custom rhythm styles, soloist AI, and microphone listening band.
- [Raw Markdown Manual](https://app.jam-a-lot.org/llms-full.txt): Complete unformatted Markdown text of the user manual for raw LLM ingestion.

## Key Capabilities & Features
- **Solo Transcription (experimental)**: Toolbox and Practice Video shortcuts open local Basic Pitch inference in a disposable CPU worker. Choose an original/authorized local audio/video file (up to 75 MB / 15 min) and a 2–180s (three-minute) passage with a concert-pitch range. One window — header, a single transport/tool bar, a continuous paper score and a slim footer — with a full-screen toggle. Play/Pause (Space) the transcribed notes, the original recording or both together from any selected note; an audio-clock cursor follows the notation/chord beat grid consistently after ½×/2× changes, with source-timed orange sounding/blue played notes and auto-scroll. Select/drag, add, erase and pan tools, 50-step undo/redo (⌘Z), selected-note pitch and seconds in the footer. Professional piano sheet music: title, composer and tempo header; printed-size clefs, key signatures and accidentals; at least two bars per line; short rests between notes shown as held/tied notes for readability; a grand staff whose treble staff is a single melody voice and whose bass staff holds everything else, switching to treble clef for bars where the left hand plays high instead of stacking ledger lines. Weaker octave ghosts are removed after transcription; notes move between staves from the footer or ⌥↑/⌥↓ (a melody note lowered under middle C moves down automatically) and Re-split staves redoes the split. There is no instrument separation, so with a band the bass staff includes the bassist. The tune's solo-form chords sit between the staves with rehearsal marks; click any bar's chord area to sync the section (A, B…) or chart bar that starts there — each sync point holds until the next, so drifting performances can be re-synced per section — otherwise alignment is automatic from the bass-staff harmony. The notation tempo starts at the recording's detected tempo (note attacks plus chart fit choose half/double time), with Detect and ½×/2× buttons. With the original recording available, Detect (and every new transcription) tracks the band's beats in the recording and puts the barlines on them, so the score follows tempo drift instead of running ahead of the chords; a Following recording chip returns to a constant tempo, and a recording without a steady pulse is reported, never fitted. Without the original, Detect uses a chart sync point to fit one local tempo while keeping its known downbeat; an uncertain anchored fit keeps existing settings. Half/double buttons keep the followed beats and the chart sync points whose barlines remain, so repeated clicks restore the same score. Private per-bar Half/Normal/Double length controls in the chord-area popup fit compressed or held measures while preserving tempo, source seconds and the tune chart; both staves, cursor, chords, Add and PDF follow actual measure starts, with local meter changes. Reset bar lengths clears corrections; global grid edits clear them, and Detect requires an explicit reset. Originals are retained automatically by hash in a private browser IndexedDB library and restored with a study; Forget saved recording removes the library copy. Quota failures are visible, and clearing site data removes recordings. Download gives letter-size sheet music as a PDF, or the private study JSON. Systems reflow to the window width, so zooming out shows more bars per line. Tune key signatures, enharmonic spelling and accidental rules are shared with Melody Staff. Save (⌘S) keeps one private per-tune browser draft; Download/Open study file round-trips private JSON without rerunning inference. Every tune source is allowed; composed tune melody gates are unchanged. Loop (L) repeats the selection or passage; Speed 100–35% slows notes and the original together with pitch kept. Download → MusicXML exports the score as shown (both hands or melody, ties, clef/meter changes, chart chords, swing marking) for MuseScore, Dorico or Sibelius. No remote source upload, MIDI export, cloud sync, public sharing or catalog writes. YouTube is for reference listening; educational use is not blanket permission to extract its audio.
- **Practice Video**: Song Info → Play Video opens a Video.js YouTube player with provider-supported/confirmed speed controls, pitch-preserving slowdown, five-second seeking and A/B phrase loops. Calculate BPM offers quarter-note tap estimates and counted A/B measurements, showing original and playback-speed BPM without changing band tempo; this is manual measurement, not audio detection. Markers and speed save locally per song/video; loops default off on reopening. Band and video playback pause each other. Loops may have a short gap; YouTube controls availability and rates. Spotify stays unchanged.
- **Tune Time Signature and 2/4 Bossa**: The Chord Editor’s Time signature selector sets the whole tune in text or grid mode; text imports preview the meter. Bossa Nova fits the complete accompaniment into two quarter-note beats, including the final pickup. `Time: 2/4` and punches such as `2.5` (& of 2) are supported.
- **Nylon Guitar Comping (Bossa Nova default)**: The Comping channel offers a level-matched nylon-string guitar (University of Iowa MIS recordings) alongside Steinway, Rhodes and tine electric piano. Bossa Nova comps on it by default; the Comping sound pick is remembered per rhythm style, and the piano-only two-hand devices are skipped on the guitar.
- **Chord Families and Modal Minor**: The piano, guitar and bass read a chord symbol as a family and move freely within it. Major is C6 = C6/9 = Cmaj7 = Cmaj9 = Cadd9. Minor is Cm7 = Cm9 = Cm11 = Cm6 (no minor-major seventh on a ii). Dominants are unaltered (7/9/13) or altered (♭9/♯9/♭13/alt), and a plain V goes altered when it resolves down a fifth. Line clichés and sus/ø/°/♯11 chords stay as written, and the chart always shows what was written. A Modal minor slider adds the So What voicing (three fourths and a major third), a grip-then-step-down call-and-response figure and a pedalling bass. Its reach grows from minor vamps to whole-bar minors, then to the ii of a ii–V.
- **Bossa, Salsa and Bolero Fills**: Short cross-stick and timbale cues, brief eighth-note chorus pickups, and spaced cadenza endings replace busy rolls. Bolero uses two-stroke cues without doubles; section arrivals replace existing percussion downbeats. Regular grooves remain intact.
- **Generated Rhythm Section**: Seeded pure-function generators for walking basslines, phrase-aware comping piano, and dynamic drums across jazz and Latin feels (Swing, Ballad, Gypsy Jazz, Bossa Nova, Samba, Salsa, Bolero, Tresillo, Soul-Jazz, Funk, EDM, Waltz). Soul Jazz, Funk, Blues Shuffle, R&B and Rock bass figures form four-bar statement-and-reply phrases and retain their authored quiet groove at Energy 0; electric/electronic octave figures sound the upper root. Tresillo layers a 3+3+2 drum-kit pulse with claves and congas. Samba is a batucada, not a kit groove: pandeiro sixteenths (thumb, fingertip ghosts, accent on the fourth), tamborim teleco-teco and a kick surdo weighted on beat 2, with energy adding players one rung at a time from the pandeiro alone at Energy 0 to the full bateria (surdo and ganzá, tamborim, caixa, agogô and cuíca, a second surdo) at 5 (CC0 recordings); samba and bossa breaks (`samba break`/`breque`, `samba convenção`, `chamada`, `virada`, `bossa break`, `bossa hits`) are text-chart keywords that stop the groove for a bar while the whole band plays the figure; the measured samba swingue puts the 3rd and 4th sixteenths of every beat early at every tempo, in drums, bass and comping alike (cut-time 4/4 or 2/4). Soul Waltz adds a modern funk / soul-jazz groove in 3/4 (backbeat on beat 3, kick on 1 and &2, six authored energy levels). Soul 6/8 adds the modern funk / soul-jazz groove in 6/8, felt in two, fitted to 3/4, 6/8, 12/8, 6/4 and 4/4 charts (backbeat on the second pulse, kick on 1 and the 6 pickup, bembé bell on the ride at Energy 4, six authored energy levels). Soul 6/8 Brushes pairs natural acoustic bass and Rhodes with a brush kit: an eight-cell bass phrase of held notes, late pickups, short chord-tone connections, quiet short plucks, deliberate rests and a low-to-upper register reply. Energy 0 uses roots every fourth chart bar on held harmony; 1 every other bar; 2 roots per cell and occasional pickups; 3 the reviewed reference-like phrase; 4–5 progressively more connecting replies and stronger touch. At 0–1 written chord changes interrupt rests, including mid-bar changes, and quiet spacing counts physical chart bars even in 12/8. Notes follow the playing chart and held roots honor written bass-note changes (seeded brush stir with longer tails and occasional soft three-stroke rolls, light shaker weave with rests, wandering kick, no kit hat or ride at Energy 0-3). Bolero modern adds a contemporary kit-and-percussion arrangement: bass on 1 and accented &2 with optional 4, prominent kick/snare and hi-hat sharing &2 with a dynamic snare answer on 4, an eighth-note ride cymbal wash entering at higher energy levels (Energy 3–5), softer hand percussion, and spacious acoustic piano at 50–110 BPM. Energy 0 preserves the bass figure; the original Bolero remains available. Salsa sections can independently select normal two-hit bell, loose quarter-note motion, or an even four-hit quarter-note bell drive at any energy level, without changing clave, tumbao, or tempo. Bolero piano develops an eight-bar statement from bordoneo, tresillo, partial-cell answers, space, and high-energy cinquillo rather than repeating a one- or two-bar loop. A Swingue knob beside the tempo (Samba only) sets the swingue depth from straight to double; agogô and cuíca are real recorded bells and batucada strokes.
- **Jazz Drummer Phrase Vocabulary**: Swing ride cymbal plays seeded eight-bar phrases with selective skip-note rests and arrival inflections while preserving quarter-note time. Snare and kick use two-bar call-and-response and accent charted offbeat chord arrivals. Acoustic section changes use bridge, return, and chorus setup figures with melodic toms. Philly Joe, Elvin, Tony, and Max have distinct ride, hi-hat, and snare pocket placement.
- **Live Changes**: Runtime-only reharmonization with strict blues/Rhythm Changes fingerprints plus destination-aware tritone, secondary-dominant, passing-diminished, backdoor, full tritone ii-V, and reviewed turnaround substitutions. Same-bar and cross-bar cadences are supported, and Flow plans a stable phrase-wide density without overlapping a written arrival. Coltrane defaults on with fixed two-, three-, and four-bar ii-V-I layouts; strict blues and Rhythm Changes can also borrow atomic Bird Blues and complete bridge families. The reviewed I–♭III–♭VI–♭II major-seventh turnaround is included; backdoor and Coltrane candidates share the cadence draw. Above 180 BPM, substitutions generate at most two chords per bar while written chart chords stay intact. Every device preserves bar count, timing, and its written arrival; same-root extensions are color rather than substitutions.
- **The Listening Band**: Real-time microphone listening engine using Web Audio FFT bin subtraction to follow soloist energy, density, and register without speaker feedback bleed.
- **Instrument Mixer**: dB-calibrated mixer with pan positioning, custom SFZ sample import, per-kit and per-rhythm-style fader memory, synthetic drum voice design, and a Mix & EQ Studio (live spectrum, draggable EQ dots and scroll bandwidth, rotary knobs, a level-matched Linear preset with default Kolmogorov -5/3 exponent, stable through zero and shortcut buttons for -1, -1/2, 0, +1/2 and +1, bus compressor, DJ filter/echo/stutter activated on tab selection, with six performance controls above the knobs; no legacy textures), plus separate bass/drum Instrument FX racks (drive, low-pass, auto-wah, chorus, phaser, delay, output trim; independent bypass and global local memory; Nordic Bass, Drum Echo and Floating Space presets inspired by e.s.t.). Tight-kick soft strokes retain their acoustic colour with smoother levels into stronger strokes. All three bass and four comping sounds have automatic phrase-level matching and tone shaping; nylon guitar includes subsonic cleanup and pluck presence.
- **Chord Chart Editors & User Tunes**: Visual grid editor and live text-mode editor supporting universal lead-sheet shorthand (`|:`, `:|`, numbered first/second endings, `N.C.`, `x4`, section labels), beat-accurate custom punches, tacet bars, and `to coda at last` directions. `Form:`, `Solos:`, `In between solos:`, and `Head out:` can name distinct section orders; the chart follows the playing form while saved text keeps its authored section order and spacing; written Intro and Coda blocks also provide enabled one-shot sections. Written endings close at a quieter energy without a new drum build. The Basie Ending is two bars (`| C Dbdim/C | C |`, struck `| 3 | 1 &2 4 |`): the piano alone plinks D F C, D# F# C, E G C, then the band hits the tonic with a big splash on beat 4; a written ending can finish with the same tag via `[Ending: basie]`, resolving in the tune's key. A leading Coda direction enters Coda before the final pass of a repeated section; a trailing direction plays its marked chord first. In a Form header, `A` plays both endings while `A[2]` goes directly to ending 2; expanded and Vintage charts show complete passes as `A[1]` / `A[2]`, and Repeat View stays folded with the active ending highlighted during playback. Clicking a displayed intro or ending bar starts or seeks at that exact one-shot bar, just like a chorus bar. A bar can carry its own quarter-note meter (for example, `| 3/4 C7 G7 |` in a 4/4 tune), and playback, seeking, metronome and notation follow its actual length. Half bars / Double bars re-spread the same chords over half or twice the bars when the chart has one meter throughout. Chord input accepts lowercase and hand-written shorthand, unreadable symbols are reported rather than dropped, and unsaved editor text is recoverable. Private edits to catalog standards remain in Jazz Standards; original and explicitly copied songs live in User Tunes.
- **Tune Sharing & Cloud Sync**: Send charts directly to `@handle`, share via links (`#share=code`) or QR code, manage an incoming Shared Tunes Inbox with preview/accept, and auto-sync user libraries across devices.
- **IP Safety Enforcement**: User-original compositions retain custom lyrics and melody notes; catalog standards strip all lyrics and melody before generating share payloads.

- Practice icon: generate major/minor ii–V–I cadences, turnarounds, dominant cycles, and Coltrane Countdown changes across fixed or random key steps. Charts save in the Practice collection and use the normal Performance Plan, drum trading, and Living Changes controls.

Desktop Toolbox: vertical toolbar centered at the left edge with all available tool icons, descriptive tooltips, piano keys for Keyboard and an EQ-curve icon distinct from Mixer; up to 1100 px retains the header menu. Hidden in full-screen performance. Neutral beta/guest styling. Instrument FX: Preset defaults to the second entry, Nordic Bass, while staying bypassed until enabled. Off racks collapse. Reset preset restores selected factory defaults or a saved snapshot, double-click restores one knob’s preset value, selected identity persists across edits/reloads, edits are marked, and New preset saves named current-rack snapshots in this browser, separately for bass and drums.

Reference groove development is separate agent-assisted local tooling (`$groove-from-audio`), not a deployed app upload feature. It uses Audio Separator, Beat This! and ADTOF to produce private stems, editable unsnapped event candidates and an audible timing sketch before a generalized accompaniment style is authored. Review controls include pulse/meter/bar-one correction, per-hit voice/time/velocity/enabled edits, filtered playback, and JSON download/reload. Optional Gemini observations are separate and unverified.

Solo Transcription defaults to local six-source piano separation (both hands, A0–C8), then a local piano-only note reader (Transkun), with Basic Pitch in the browser as the fallback. Separation needs npm run solo:server after bash scripts/groove/setup.sh (Vite mounts the helper during development); without the helper the panel selects Whole recording (no separation) and says so, so the online app transcribes without it. A requested separation never silently falls back to the mix. Transient isolated piano playback/WAV download, Both hands / Melody only score and PDF views, and joint onset/release rounding reduce fragmented notation. Model output may contain bleed, missed or wrong notes; no remote audio upload.

Solo Transcription keyboard editing (MuseScore layout): ←/→ step through notes, ⇧ extends a range, ⌘←/→ jumps bars, ⌘A selects all; A–G repitches to the nearest letter in the key signature; ↑/↓ semitone and ⌘↑/↓ octave transpose the selection; ⌥↑/↓ move staves; 3–7 set sixteenth–whole lengths and . toggles a dot; Delete lands on the next note; N toggles Add; Esc clears the selection. One undo step per edit; optional note audition on select/edit; in-dialog shortcut list. Swing notation: Straight/Swing 8ths writes swung eighths as straight eighths (display only, Swing marking beside the tempo, auto-detected for new transcriptions; sixteenths unchanged). Cleanup tools: Requantize (Q; 1/8, 1/16 or Swing 8ths at the passage's measured offbeat, from each bar's beat 1; folds doubled unisons; rewrites saved timing, undoable), split at cursor (/), join (J), tie to next same pitch (+), copy/cut/paste in beats at the cursor (⌘C/⌘X/⌘V); the footer edits Bar, Beat and Length in beats.

Solo Transcription beat alignment: Beat 1 at (seconds), Selected note = beat 1, and Reset beat alignment shift the score grid without shifting audio or dropping earlier notes. Opening partial bars are preserved; both hands, playback cursor, note editing and PDF use the shifted grid. Saved study notation.downbeatSeconds retains alignment. Grid changes clear chart sync points.

Rhythm Lab → Microrhythm opens inline below the chart. One aligned chart combines timing interpolation/extrapolation and 1–128 realized bars (default 16), with a vertical λ slider beside the first diagram. The chosen cycle length persists and drives playback too; long plots scroll. Base rhythm offers Minimal (two/three kit sounds: kick, hi-hat, cross-stick, with sparse coordinated bass and comping) and experimental Swing/Samba/Bossa Nova copies. Bossa retains its native kit, shaker, bass and guitar comping with whole-band authored timing. Swing lists two/three-interval studies, Samba/Bossa four-interval studies, Minimal all studies. Samba choices include Samba swingue, Escola de Samba da Cidade, Gal Costa, Rogê, Chico Buarque, Innov Gnawa’s Chorfa, Muthallith, Sʿadāwī, Waaju’s Fangara and two Rollando passages; screenshot-only choices are removed. Rollando alternates measured pulses within each bar and its contrast scales with λ. λ extends nominally from −1 to 2, bounded before any interval collapses; the extended plot shades extrapolation and marks A=0/B=1. Effect strength is removed. Samba λ=1/2 matches built-in Swingue at 100%/200%, with its compact control hidden during the experiment. The selected base drives the main band even on a chart with another feel. A highlighted strip at the bottom names affected players. Blue handles edit ±1σ; across-bar odd/even offsets, correlation, New realization and realized statistics expose the seeded clock. Changes auto-apply to upcoming bars. Playback highlighting follows the main transport. Throughout the app, when the chart and stage are out of view, a floating Chord changes panel reuses the stage’s rolling renderer and played chords (including Living Changes, intros and endings); it freezes when paused and closes when either display returns. User-style JSON retains both ordinary and alternating-pulse timing cycles.
